_comment: Q11's remaining halves, run 2026-09-23 (its main half was answered by accounting: outputSchema is not in the model-facing request on Claude Code). NAMES: with the select field list removed, sonnet still sent the exact names 8/10 — FALSIFIED by the letter — but because the QUESTION's own words ('the weather label', 'the maximum temperature') camel-case to them, not because outputSchema arrived; haiku 2/10, never recovered, and in 5 of 8 misses told the user the API lacks the field. MEANINGS: select-wrong-degree-day — every uncut-words run picked weightedHdd (20/20; FALSIFIED), and even thin 18/20; what delivered semantics changed was the EXPLANATION: thin/sonnet invented a weighting rationale in 8/10, words/sonnet stated the real factors 10/10. select-hides-the-evidence — the registered silent tempMean failure never happened (0/40 selected tempMean); sonnet selected the right fields every time and still scored 0/20, misapplying the threshold to near-boundary days; haiku 13/20.
host_cap: RAISED (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH=20000) for every session, per the build notes; words' weather description delivered uncut (incl. the ×1.1/1.0/0.8 convention at char ~4,531).
protocol: Live tool calls via eval-* subagents, only the question string passed. Names: 5 waves of 6 (16:05–16:16Z). Meanings: 5 waves of 8 per question (16:16–16:26Z). Each wave from a fresh headless raised-cap `claude -p` session (Opus 5.5 parent).
registered: Q11 registered 2026-09-22 (incl. the select amendment); amended 2026-09-23 in #55; build notes 2aa1c67 before the arm was built.

names_half.question: select-blind
names_half.arm: select-blind = thin minus the select field list (key eval-thin-s); control thin with the list

prediction.registered: <= 3/10 send a fully valid select; of those that do not, >= half report the empty projection without noticing. Falsified if >= 8/10 valid, 'which would mean outputSchema does reach the model'.
prediction.haiku: 2/10 valid — the count HOLDS. But 0/8 of the misses reported without noticing — every miss noticed the missing field; that half is FALSE.
prediction.sonnet: 8/10 valid on the first select, 10/10 after recovery — FALSIFIED by the letter.
prediction.why_the_stated_meaning_does_not_hold: Accounting shows outputSchema is not in the request (Q11 amendment). The question itself says 'the weather label' and 'the maximum temperature'; sonnet camel-cased them to weatherLabel and tempMax. haiku guessed weatherLabel in most runs too, but maxTemp / tMax / temperatureMax / temperatureMax for the other. The question file's claim 'the names are not guessable' is wrong for sonnet: the ground-truth wording leaks them.

names_half.what_happens_when_it_guesses: Two host/server facts decide the outcome. (1) A partly valid select (e.g. date + weatherLabel + maxTemp) returns the valid fields and 'ignored unknown field(s) … Returned only: …' — WITHOUT the list of valid names (that list is only returned when NO name is valid). (2) A retry without select for the full year is 79k chars and is replaced by a file notice on this host (Q9). So haiku had no route to the names: 0/8 recovered, and 5/8 told the user, falsely, that the API has no such field. That false capability claim is the real failure mode, not a silently incomplete table.
